attempts.text:
```json
{
  "map": true,
  "subject": {
    "columns": ["protein_id"],
    "resolver": "pharos_protein_gene",
    "category": "biolink:Gene"
  },
  "object": {
    "columns": ["trait"],
    "resolver": "pattern:OMIM:Phenotype: .*?(\\d{6}) \\(\\d\\)",
    "category": "biolink:Disease"
  },
  "predicate": "biolink:gene_associated_with_condition",
  "association_category": "biolink:GeneToDiseaseAssociation",
  "knowledge_level": "knowledge_assertion",
  "agent_type": "manual_agent",
  "primary_knowledge_source": "infores:omim",
  "qualifiers": {},
  "edge_properties": ["trait"],
  "keep_if": {
    "column": "trait",
    "matches": "Phenotype: .*\\d{6} \\(\\d\\)",
    "reason": "A trait that holds only 'MIM Number: N' gives the gene's own OMIM entry and no phenotype. A phenotype written without a phenotype MIM number gives no disease identifier. Either way there is no gene-to-condition claim to assert."
  },
  "split_by": null,
  "by_value": null,
  "notes": "The object is the phenotype MIM number: the six digits just before the OMIM mapping key, as in '(3)'. The leading 'MIM Number' is the gene's entry, not a disease. The trait is kept as an edge property so the mapping key and the phenotype name are preserved. The predicate is gene_associated_with_condition rather than causes because the trait can include somatic, susceptibility and provisional entries."
}
```
